- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the early-period lows to reflect market resilience.  
- After a recent price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward — apply a 3–5 day lagged mean reversion buffer to avoid premature drop.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6) and forecast is volatile, smooth transitions by averaging 3–5 prior days’ values before projecting.  
- Model consistently overestimates short-term declines (especially after negative sentiment) — adjust downward bias by 2–4% for 3–7 day horizons.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence in continuation.
